findings.issue_text: [High/security] canManage(ClientModel) omits the inherited isInternal(client) guard, allowing a Clients/manage grant to manage protected internal clients such as realm-management.
[Medium/bug] A global manage grant does not satisfy canView(), so inherited canList() prevents administrators who can manage all clients from listing clients.

[Medium/api] canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException despite its boolean authorization-check contract, causing FGAP V2 token-exchange requests to return a server error instead of a clean denial.
[Medium/data] The feature-flag wrapper prevents role, client, and group removal cleanup when FGAP V2 is disabled, leaving orphaned legacy FGAP authorization resources and policies.

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: [Medium/data] The feature-flag wrapper prevents role, client, and group removal cleanup when FGAP V2 is disabled, leaving orphaned legacy FGAP authorization resources and policies.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments identify the same core issue: the feature flag guarding the permission cleanup logic in AdminPermissions event listener is inconsistent, leading to orphaned permissions/resources when certain feature flag combinations are used. The golden comment says V1 flag is used when V2 should be (or cleanup should happen regardless), while the candidate says cleanup doesn't happen when V2 is disabled. Both are pointing to the same fundamental bug - the feature flag inconsistency causing orphaned permission data during role/client/group removal. The candidate's description is slightly different in framing (focusing on V2 being disabled vs V1 being used incorrectly), but they're identifying the same underlying problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] canManage(ClientModel) omits the inherited isInternal(client) guard, allowing a Clients/manage grant to manage protected internal clients such as realm-management.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for ClientPermissionsV2.java, the canManage(ClientModel client) method at lines 68-71 only checks `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)` and `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Comparing this to the parent class ClientPermissions (not fully shown but referenced), the V2 implementation appears to omit the `isInternal(client)` guard that would protect internal/system clients like realm-management from being managed. The finding correctly identifies that the new V2 implementation lacks this security check that exists in the base implementation, potentially allowing users with Clients/manage permission to manage protected internal clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] A global manage grant does not satisfy canView(), so inherited canList() prevents administrators who can manage all clients from listing clients.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, canList() in ClientPermissionsV2 is not overridden, so it inherits from ClientPermissions. The finding claims that canManage() returning true wouldn't satisfy canView() for listing purposes. However, examining the code: canManage() checks root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) OR hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). The canView() method checks canViewClientDefault() OR hasPermission(VIEW). The canList() method (inherited) likely checks canView() plus query roles. The issue is that having MANAGE permission doesn't automatically grant VIEW permission in canView(). However, this appears to be intentional design - MANAGE and VIEW are separate scopes. The finding assumes MANAGE should imply VIEW for listing, but this is a design choice, not necessarily a bug. The tests in the diff show testManageAllClients() successfully lists clients after getting MANAGE permission, suggesting the implementation works correctly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException despite its boolean authorization-check contract, causing FGAP V2 token-exchange requests to return a server error instead of a clean denial.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo() throws UnsupportedOperationException. This method is part of the ClientPermissionEvaluator interface which has a boolean return type contract for authorization checks. When token-exchange functionality calls this method in FGAP V2 mode, it will get an exception instead of a boolean authorization result, causing a server error rather than a proper authorization denial. This is a real defect - the method should return false or implement proper V2 authorization logic, not throw an exception that breaks the interface contract.
